newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico mulls $200 million dual-rate note issue.
newsitem.headline: Mexico mulls $200 million dual-rate note issue.

text.p: Mexico may issue around $200 million in dual-rate notes that would help it pay off a previous $1.5 billion dual-rate issue that comes due in November, officials and news reports said on Tuesday.
"We will place an instrument with similar characteristics if conditions are favorable," said one Finance Ministry official. He noted the new issue would not be exactly the same as the previous one.
No time frame was given for the issue. "It depends on how we evaluate the market at the time."
Last November, the federal government placed the outstanding $1.5 billion one-year note.
The note gave investors a choice between a coupon of the 12-month LIBOR or the 28-Cetes rate less six percentage points. It can be redeemed in either Mexican pesos or U.S. dollars.

Mexico has so far placed around $1.3 billion in debt to pay for the issue coming due. In August, Mexico offered a German mark issue worth about $660 million, and in September a Japanese yen bond worth about $640 million.
The Mexico City newspaper La Reforma quoted a Finance Ministry official as saying that any new dual-rate note issue would cover the remaining amount of the dual-rate note coming due and interest.
